title: A Rose from Homer's Grave
summary: On the sun-drenched coast of Smyrna, beside the blue waters of the Aegean Sea, an ancient tumulus rises beneath fragrant pines. The local folk say it is the tomb of Homer—the blind...
full_text:
On the sun-drenched coast of Smyrna, beside the blue waters of the Aegean Sea, an ancient tumulus rises beneath fragrant pines. The local folk say it is the tomb of Homer—the blind father of epic song.

Upon the mound grew a bush of deep crimson roses. A nightingale sang in the branches every twilight, pouring out melodies of Achilles' wrath, Hector's noble courage, and the wooden horse of Troy.

A pilgrim from the distant northern snows visited the tomb. Revering the immortal poet whose songs had illuminated his youth, the traveler plucked a single blooming rose, pressed it reverently within a volume of the Iliad, and carried it back across stormy seas to his quiet northern study.

Years rolled by; the rose dried and lost its fresh petals, but whenever the reader opened the book, the fragrance of ancient Greece breathed forth into the cold winter air. Empires crumble, cities fall to dust, and marble statues decay; but the poetry of the human soul, like the rose from Homer's tomb, blooms in eternal spring.
moral: True poetry outlives empires and monuments, blooming forever in the memory of mankind.
